Oral Judgment :
1.
The issue involved in this appeal is accident occurred due to sole negligence of the driver of Maruti Van.

sentences.text: 1 2. It is contention of learned counsel for the appellant /Insurance S.S.Kilaje 14-FA-1823-2019- Judgment (C).doc Company that the truck was standing on the side of the road.
The Maruti Van driver gave dash to the stationed truck.

The accident occurred due to sole negligence of the driver of Maruti van but this fact is not considered by the Tribunal and has fixed only 50% contributory negligence on the driver of Maruti van, which is erroneous.

He is sole responsible for the accident,
hence requested to allow the appeal.
3. It is contention of learned counsel for respondent Nos.1, 2 and 4/ claimants that the offending truck was parked on the road without tail lamps / indicator.
The accident occurred at 4:00 a.m.
The accident occurred due to sole negligence of the driver of offending truck but these facts are not considered by the Tribunal.
Learned counsel further submitted that the Tribunal has awarded consortium amount to only one claimant.

So compensation be given to the rest of the claimants and requested to dismiss the appeal.
4.
I have heard both the learned counsel.
Perused the Judgment and Order passed by the Motor Accident Claims Tribunal, Pune (for short "the Tribunal").
It is claimants' case that the deceased along with his family was proceeding towards Pune in Maruti Van bearing registration No.MAM- 992.
The brother-in-law of the deceased was driving the vehicle in moderate speed and in accordance with the rules of the traffic.

While the said car reached near Shubham Hotel, at Koregaon, the road widening S.S.Kilaje 14-FA-1823-2019- Judgment (C).doc work was in progress and on a blind turning point of the road, truck bearing registration No. MP-17-C-0862 was parked without the parking lights and since it was night time, the driver of the Maruti van could not locate the truck and gave dash to it in which the deceased died.
The offence was registered against the driver of Maruti van.
To prove the negligence of truck driver.
the claimants have relied on police papers and has examined the claimant No.1, Shubhangi Baviskar.
At the time of accident she was travelling in the said Maruti van.
She has stated that the lights of the truck were not on and that road widening work was going on and on a blind turn, the said truck was parked.
Nothing elicited in her cross examination.
5. Considering evidence on record, as well as the deceased was the owner of the Maruti van, the Tribunal has considered 50% contributory negligence of the deceased.
The claimants have not challenged the findings of the Tribunal.
It is contention of learned counsel for the Insurance company that the truck was parked on the side of the road and it was sole negligence of the driver of Maruti van.
The documents produced on record shows that accident occurred at 4:00 a.m., it was dark.
The truck was stationed on the road without putting indicator or parking lights on.
The spot where accident occurred, was blind spot.
The widening work of the road was going on, accident occurred on the curve so driver of S.S.Kilaje 14-FA-1823-2019- Judgment (C).doc
Maruti van could not see the truck due to dark and it was without parking lights or indicator.

Though, it is contention of learned counsel for the appellant /Insurance Company that it was parked on the side of the road,
but widening work of the road was going on.

Moreover, as per the Central Vehicles Rules, if the vehicle is stationed on the road, proper precautions have to be taken by the driver of the truck by putting indicator, tail lamps or parking lights on, but it was not taken.

Section 15 of the said Rules reads thus:

2 " Section 15 in the Rules of the Road Regulations, 1989:
15. Parking of the vehicle:-
(1) Every driver of a motor vehicle parking on any road shall park in such a way that it does not cause or is not likely to cause danger, obstruction or undue inconvenience to other road users and the manner of parking is indicated by any sign board or markings on the road side, he shall park his vehicle in such manner.

sentences.text:
( i). the hazard warning lights of the vehicle shall be switched on immediately;
(ii). on highways and major roads with fast speed, reflective traffic warning triangles shall be placed at a distance of fifty meters behind the broken-down vehicle; and In present case, it shows that the driver of the said Truck has clearly violated all the rules and regulations of the Central Motor Vehicle Rules, Motor Vehicle Rules and the Rules of the Road and Regulation, 1989, and Regulations made under the Act."
"When any vehicle is stationed on the road at night time, as per Rule 109 of the Central Motor Vehicles Rules, 1989, proper precautions are necessary to be taken.

It reads thus:-
109. Parking light:-
[Every construction equipment vehicle, combine harvester and motor vehicle] and every motor vehicle other than motor cycles and three wheeled invalid carriages shall be provided with one white or amber parking light on each side in the front.
In addition to the front lights, two red parking lights one on each side in the rear shall be provided.

The front and rear parking lights shall remain lit even when the vehicle is kept stationary on the road:
Provided that these rear lamps can be the same as the rear lamps referred to in rule 105 sub-rule (2): [Provided also that construction equipment vehicles [and combined harvesters], which are installed with food light lamps or sports lights at the front,
rear or side of the vehicle for their off highway or construction operations, shall have separate control for such lamps or lights and these shall be permanently switched of when the vehicle is travelling on the road.]"
In the present case, it has come on record that the indicator and tail lamps of offending vehicle were not on.
The driver of the offending truck did not step into the witness box to prove this fact.
Considering the above facts, I do not see merit in the contention of learned counsel for the appellant/ Insurance Company that accident occurred due to sole negligence of the driver of Maruti van.
S.S.Kilaje 14-FA-1823-2019- Judgment (C).doc
The Tribunal has awarded consortium amount of Rs.40,000/- to one claimant.
There are 4 claimants.
Hence rest of the 3 claimants are entitled for consortium amount.
As per the view of Hon'ble Apex Court in the case of Magma General Insurance Co. Ltd. vs. Nanu Ram, 2018 ACJ 2782 (SC) , each claimant is entitled for Rs.48,000/- as consortium amount.

ORDER (a) The appeal is dismissed.

(c) The appellant/Insurance Company shall deposit enhanced amount along with interest within six weeks.
(d) The respondent Nos.1,2 and 4 /claimants are permitted to withdraw the enhanced amount along with accrued interest thereon.
(d) The respondent Nos.1,2 and 4/ claimants shall pay deficit court fees on the enhanced amount as per rule.
(e) The statutory amount be transmitted to the Tribunal along with accrued interest thereon.
The parties are at liberty to withdraw it as per Rule.
(f) R & P be sent back to the Tribunal.
(g) All pending applications, if any, also disposed of.
